speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long this painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg has been present? Also, have you noticed any changes in its appearance or any discharge?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease, is the lesion raised with undermined edges and a "punched-out" appearance? Also, have you experienced any joint pain or recent eye inflammation since this started?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of recent travel to areas where spider bites or tropical ulcers are common? Also, are you currently experiencing any systemic symptoms like fever or chills?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Doctor: Given your recent travel to Wisconsin and the lesion's appearance, have you noticed any other redness spreading outward from the bite site, or have you had any muscle aches or fatigue? I also need to know if you have taken any antibiotics for this yet.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the lesion's appearance, have you noticed any other ulcers in your mouth or on your genitals? I would like to REQUEST TEST: Skin biopsy and REQUEST IMAGES of the lesion to rule out pyoderma gangrenosum.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy Histopathology: Neutrophilic infiltration without infection, consistent with pyoderma gangrenosum.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results confirming neutrophilic infiltration without infection, combined with your history of Crohn's disease and the lesion's appearance, are diagnostic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
